name: Outcome-Oriented Predictive Process Monitoring
description: Predictive business process monitoring refers to the act of making predictions about the future state of ongoing cases of a business process, based on their incomplete execution traces and logs of historical (completed) traces. Motivated by the increasingly pervasive availability of fine-grained event data about business process executions, the problem of predictive process monitoring has received substantial attention in the past years. In particular, a considerable number of methods have been put forward to address the problem of outcome-oriented predictive process monitoring, which refers to classifying each ongoing case of a process according to a given set of possible categorical outcomes - e.g., Will the customer complain or not? Will an order be delivered, canceled or withdrawn? reputation: A well-known line of work in predictive process monitoring that helped standardize outcome-oriented evaluation, though results are fragmented across datasets and settings.
notes: Benchmarking is complicated by heterogeneous datasets, protocols, and baselines across papers; not a single unified leaderboard and often non-LLM methods dominate.
